## Phase D gate — enforced from inside the test suite

`tests/c3_boundaries.rs::phase_d_symbol_parity` re-runs `nm -D --defined-only`
on the C `.so` at test time and `dlsym`s **every** exported symbol against the
Rust `.so`. It fails with the full list if any symbol is unresolvable.

Latest run:

```
symbol parity: 878 C symbols, 0 missing from Rust
```

`tests/c3_boundaries.rs::phase_d_all_getters_agree` additionally *calls* every
zero-argument constant getter in the library through both `.so` files and
compares the results:

```
getters compared: 322 size_t, 15 int/uchar, 19 string
```

Two symbols match the `*_bytes` naming pattern but take arguments and are
therefore excluded from the blind-call sweep (they are covered by the normal
differential tests): `crypto_core_keccak1600_extract_bytes` and
`crypto_core_keccak1600_xor_bytes`.

## Feature combinations

`translation/Cargo.toml` declares **no `[features]` section**, and the sources
contain **no `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`**, so the crate has exactly one
configuration. `verify_all.sh` derives the combination list mechanically from
`Cargo.toml` and reports this; if features are ever added, it will loop over
`--no-default-features`, each single feature, and `--all-features`
automatically.

The project also builds **no binary target** (no `[[bin]]`, no `src/main.rs`, no
`src/bin/`, and `c_src/CMakeLists.txt` has no `add_executable`), so there is no
stdout comparison to make.

## Nothing was stubbed

No symbol in the Rust `.so` is a stub, `unimplemented!()`, or a placeholder:
every one of the 878 shared symbols is exercised either by a behavioural
differential test or by the getter sweep above. The 12 extra Rust symbols are
the `sodium_runtime_has_*` CPU-feature probes, which the portable C build
compiles out of its export set; they are additive, not divergent.
